DI G BACONC PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. JUL 03 Hon. RONALD B. COSICO Municipal Mayor Paete, Laguna Dear Mayor Cosico: This refers to your letter dated January 5, 2024, concerning the propriety of the action of the sanggunian vis-å-vis the 2024 Executive Budget of Paete. Hereunder are the pertinent factual antecedents as culled in your letter and its attachments: • • On November 16, 2023, the herein concerned sanggunian held its Budget Hearing. In the said Hearing, there have been discussions regarding some plantilla positions, which are included in the Budget Proposal submitted by the Office of the Mayor. On December 5, 2023, the Sangguniang Committee on Whole held a Hearing in connection with the proposed Executive Budget. Accordingly, after various Committee Hearings, the Sangguniang Bayan deemed it proper to recommend certain transfer of funds. However, they introduced new items to the Executive Budget. In its undated letter addressed to the Office of the Local Chief Executive (LCE), the sanggunian recommended revisions or amendments to the 2024 Annual Budget. The said amendments and introduction of new items was stated in Resolution No. 246, s. 2023 but was not included in Appropriation Ordinance No. 2023- 004. You approved and signed Appropriation Ordinance No. 2023-004 without the inclusion of the amendments as stated in Resolution No. 246, s. 2023. Hence, you are now seeking guidance from the Department in aid of any rebuttal that may be instituted by the Sangguniang Bayan regarding the amendments that they would like to incorporate in the Executive Budget. Foremost, attention is respectfully invited to Article 415 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (herein after referred to as the Code), thus: "Article 415. Budget Authorization. — The local sanggunian may not increase the proposed amount in the executive budget nor include new items except to provide for statutory and contractual obligations but in no case shall it exceed the total appropriations in the executive budget." "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

The foregoing provision is reiterated in Item 4.5, Chapter Ill Of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Budget Operations Manual for LGUs: "4.5 Limitations on Legislative Action. — The Sanggunian may not increase the proposed amount in the executive budget nor include new items except to provide for statutory and contractual obligations that may not have been considered in the preparation of the budget or that the amounts provided may be deficient. In no case, however, shall such additional provision result to the excess of the total appropriations over the proposed in the executive budget." As could be clearly gleaned from the aforequoted provision, the inclusion of new items not found in the executive budget is prohibited. This prohibition, however, is not absolute—the Code provides clear exceptions to statutory and contractual obligations that were omitted or may have been overlooked in the preparation of the executive budget, provided that said insertion should not result in an excess of the total appropriations of the executive budget. Relatedly, in our previous opinions, we clarified that 'statutory obligations' are those demandable obligations derived from an express provision of law. Meanwhile, 'contractual obligations' pertain to those obligations incurred by virtue of contracts entered into by the local chief executive pursuant to Section 22(c) of the Code, that were authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets of the preceding year 1. In the herein case, it is well to note that the herein concerned sanggunian—through its letter addressed to the Office of the LCE—recommends the revisions of some items in the Executive Budget. In particular, it recommends the deletion of plantilla positions (i.e., Engineering II; Private Secretary I; Labor Employment Officer Ill; and Local Economic Development and Investment Promotion Officer), and in lieu thereof, it introduces new items ((i.e., Special Program for Employment of Student; Teacher's Month; Assistance to Bantay Bayan; Gas and Fuel Expenses; and Training and Seminar) that it finds more important and needs appropriation. Here, we find the opinion rendered by the DBM in L-B2001-06 pertinent. In it, the DBM opined that the power of the sanggunian to approve and appropriate an annual budget carries with it the power to slash the same, as proposed by the LCE. However, the DBM reiterates the provision found in Article 415 of the IRR of the Code that the sanggunian may only introduce new items in the annual budget if the said items fall within the purview of 'statutory and contractual obligations' as above-discussed. In view of the foregoing, this Department is of the opinion that the action of the concerned sanggunian in introducing new items/revisions appears to be untenable, as these items do not fall within the exceptions categorically provided by the Code. At any rate, in line with the Department's supervisory function over local governments, we would like to reiterate some of the fundamental principles that should govern the financial affairs, transactions, and operations of local government pursuant to Section 305 of the Code, thus: • Local governments shall formulate sound financial plans, and local budgets shall be based on functions, activities, and projects, in terms of expected results; 1 DILG Legal Opinion No. 20, s. 2014, dated June 3, 2014. Page 2 of 3

• • Local budget plans and goals shall, as far as practicable, be harmonized with national development plans, goals, and strategies in order to optimize the utilization of resources and to avoid duplication in the use of fiscal and physical resources; Local govemment units shall ensure that their respective budgets incorporate the requirements of their component units and provide for equitable allocation of resources among these component units; Fiscal responsibility shall be shared by all those exercising authority over the financial affairs, transactions, and operations of the local government units; and The local government unit shall endeavor to have a balanced budget in each fiscal year of operation." This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
